quote: The reference `purepy` tool is a static verifier. It MUST NOT import or execute analyzed project code.
notes: Sentinel files prove that rejected project statements and accepted manifest-backed imports do not execute project or host code.

quote: Later language levels MAY add features, but they MUST preserve the guarantees of accepted PurePy 0.1 programs. New features MUST be independently specified and MUST NOT retroactively reinterpret unsupported PurePy 0.1 syntax as trusted behavior.
notes: Future language evolution obligation. Only PurePy 0.1 is implemented; preserving prior semantics across future versions is not established by the present tests.

quote: When the verifier cannot establish the exact meaning of an operation, it MUST reject the operation.
notes: Exact operations and unknown-operation/suppression rejection have direct controls. Bounded generated semantic pairs require acceptance and specific rejection codes; arbitrary-source fuzzing checks parser-to-checker integrity, spans, and worker determinism. These short campaigns do not establish all syntax/semantic combinations or replace independent soundness review.

quote: Unknown behavior MUST NOT be downgraded to a warning, inferred as pure, or authorized by a broad suppression comment.
notes: Exact operations and unknown-operation/suppression rejection have direct controls. Bounded generated semantic pairs require acceptance and specific rejection codes; arbitrary-source fuzzing checks parser-to-checker integrity, spans, and worker determinism. These short campaigns do not establish all syntax/semantic combinations or replace independent soundness review.

quote: External authority MUST enter verified code as a capability parameter supplied by the host or by another verified caller that already possesses the capability.
notes: Tests establish direct parameter forwarding and representative construction/storage/ambient-call rejection. Host entrypoint argument provenance remains trusted.

notes: Finite static tests cannot prove observational equivalence, exception determinism, or divergence for arbitrary programs. These guarantees additionally rely on Python/platform behavior, sealed operations, runtime support, and truthful trusted external declarations.

quote: 2. terminate through the same deterministic runtime exception class under the same operation and equivalent operands; or
notes: Finite static tests cannot prove observational equivalence, exception determinism, or divergence for arbitrary programs. These guarantees additionally rely on Python/platform behavior, sealed operations, runtime support, and truthful trusted external declarations.

quote: 3. fail to terminate.
notes: Finite static tests cannot prove observational equivalence, exception determinism, or divergence for arbitrary programs. These guarantees additionally rely on Python/platform behavior, sealed operations, runtime support, and truthful trusted external declarations.

quote: The outcome MUST NOT depend on ambient state.

notes: Finite static tests cannot prove observational equivalence, exception determinism, or divergence for arbitrary programs. These guarantees additionally rely on Python/platform behavior, sealed operations, runtime support, and truthful trusted external declarations.

quote: Every function parameter and return value MUST have an explicit type annotation.
notes: Explicit primitive annotations are accepted; independently missing parameter and return annotations are rejected.

quote: Every `@value` field MUST have an explicit type annotation.
notes: Annotated record fields are accepted; a bare class-body field name cannot substitute for an annotation.

quote: Module constants MUST have an explicit `Final[T]` annotation.
notes: Final constants with constant initializers are accepted; plain annotations and missing initializers reject.

quote: PurePy 0.1 rejects:
notes: The table rejects named dynamic/mutable/iterator/coroutine/union/fixed-tuple annotations. Unsupported names alone do not exhaust every possible spelling or recursive alias form.

quote: PurePy 0.1 uses exact nominal type matching, except for the explicit optional form `T | None` and the ordinary relation that a value of type `T` may be used where `T | None` is expected.
notes: Distinct structurally identical records and bool/int arguments do not subtype; the optional exception has positive controls.

quote: Every later assignment to the same name MUST have the same exact type.
notes: Includes regression for declared types lost after a returning branch. Flow joins now preserve declaration types independently of continuing-path assignment/refinement facts.

quote: A local MUST be definitely assigned on every path before use.
notes: Tests cover both-branch assignment, annotated-but-unassigned locals, use before local definition, empty loops, and continue paths; conservative loop narrowing remains an implementation choice.

quote: Branch joins MUST agree on the exact type of every live local.
notes: Same-type branch assignments pass; conflicting declared types fail, including a declaration confined to a returning branch.

notes: Deep tuple, optional, and nested-record Pure Value fields pass; fields of both capability and host-reference types reject explicitly. Targeted dynamically generated subtests: Read_record_field, Connection_record_field.

notes: Positional field order and explicit keyword construction pass; missing, wrong-type, unknown, duplicate, and unpacked arguments reject.

notes: Top-level functions can construct new immutable records from field reads; record-local behaviors and descriptors reject.

quote: Nested functions and lambdas are prohibited.
notes: Only top-level direct-call behavior remains accepted.

notes: The fixed annotated signature is the positive control. Rejections cover defaults, positional/keyword markers, variadics, type parameters, and decorators; mandatory annotation cases are mapped separately.

quote: Capability and host-reference parameters MUST retain their original names and MUST NOT be rebound.
notes: Original parameter names forward directly; rebinding and aliases of both capability and host-reference parameters reject. Targeted dynamically generated subtests: Connection_rebound.

quote: Every verified function MUST return a Pure Value type or `None`.
notes: Pure Value/None returns and source-level returns of both authority categories have direct tests. Ephemeral/function/module/class/coroutine return bans are partly enforced by rejecting their source expressions or annotations; this is not a complete return-expression matrix. Targeted dynamically generated subtests: Read_returned, Connection_returned.

quote: A call expression MUST name its target directly through a statically resolved imported or local symbol.
notes: Direct same-module/imported calls pass. Call-through-local, conditional target selection, and instance method calls reject.

quote: No other module-level statement is permitted.
notes: Accepted static declarations are contrasted with executable bootstrap and conditional-import statements.

quote: The verifier resolves imports without executing them.
notes: A sentinel host module remains unexecuted when its manifest-backed import is accepted; executable project source also rejects without execution.

quote: The initializer MUST be a constant expression consisting only of:
notes: Accepted source exercises primitive/tuple/earlier/imported/record constant forms. Ordinary calls, computed initializers, and use-before-initialization references are rejected by explicit cases.

quote: - primitive literals;
notes: Accepted source exercises primitive/tuple/earlier/imported/record constant forms. Ordinary calls, computed initializers, and use-before-initialization references are rejected by explicit cases.

quote: - tuple displays of constant expressions;
notes: Accepted source exercises primitive/tuple/earlier/imported/record constant forms. Ordinary calls, computed initializers, and use-before-initialization references are rejected by explicit cases.

quote: - references to earlier constants in the same module;
notes: Accepted source exercises primitive/tuple/earlier/imported/record constant forms. Ordinary calls, computed initializers, and use-before-initialization references are rejected by explicit cases.

quote: - references to imported verified constants; and
notes: Accepted source exercises primitive/tuple/earlier/imported/record constant forms. Ordinary calls, computed initializers, and use-before-initialization references are rejected by explicit cases.

quote: - direct construction of a `@value` record from constant expressions.
notes: Accepted source exercises primitive/tuple/earlier/imported/record constant forms. Ordinary calls, computed initializers, and use-before-initialization references are rejected by explicit cases.

quote: No ordinary function call is permitted during module initialization.
notes: Record constant construction passes while ordinary project/intrinsic initializer calls reject.

quote: Module rebinding, caches, registries, counters, and mutable containers are prohibited.
notes: Static immutable constants pass; module-name writes and mutable displays reject. Dedicated registry/cache examples are represented by the same forbidden syntax.

quote: Augmented assignment such as `+=` is prohibited because Python may dispatch to in-place mutation.
notes: Explicit same-type local rebinding passes; += rejects.

quote: Conditions MUST have exact type `bool`.
notes: Exact boolean conditions pass; primitive/tuple truthiness rejects in if, conditional expression, and while contexts.

quote: `for ... else` is prohibited.
notes: Ordinary approved for loops pass while loop else clauses reject.

quote: A `while` condition MUST have exact type `bool`.
notes: The while_loop fixture supplies the bool-loop positive control; an integer while condition is rejected.

quote: `while ... else` is prohibited.
notes: While loop rejection has a dedicated control; positive bool while behavior is also covered by the while_loop fixture.

quote: Every reachable return expression MUST match the exact declared return type.
notes: Returns preserve exact primitive types and the explicitly allowed T-to-optional relation. Non-None fallthrough and wrong return values reject.

quote: Falling off the end is permitted only for a function declared to return `None`.
notes: None fallthrough is accepted; a possible int fallthrough rejects.

quote: Discarding a non-`None` result is prohibited.
notes: Both sync and awaited non-None results must be consumed; None calls can be expression statements.

quote: Heterogeneous tuples are prohibited. Use a `@value` record instead.
notes: Homogeneous nested tuples and records pass; int/bool heterogeneous tuple rejects.

quote: The empty tuple has no standalone inferred element type. It is permitted only when an explicit contextual type supplies `tuple[T, ...]`, for example `items: tuple[int, ...] = ()`.
notes: Return/call/nested tuple context supplies the exact element type; contextless assignment rejects.

quote: List, dictionary, set, and mutable-container displays are prohibited.
notes: Immutable tuple displays pass; mutable display forms reject.

quote: `and`, `or`, and `not` operate only on exact `bool` operands and produce `bool`.
notes: All three boolean operators reject non-bool operands; bool-producing expressions compose successfully.

quote: Identity operators `is` and `is not` are permitted only with `None`.
notes: Identity requires exact None on one side and any Pure Value on the other, checked independently for each chain pair. Tests cover nonoptional/optional primitives and tuples, nominal and opaque values, typed None expressions, literal-only narrowing, reassignment, and cache/worker equivalence. A finite CPython matrix checks explicit Boolean outcomes and rejects pairs without exact None; authority, ephemerals, declarations, and unsealed equality remain prohibited.

quote: Indices must be `int`. Slice bounds must be `int | None`. Extended slicing and user-defined `__getitem__` dispatch are prohibited.
notes: Optional int slice bounds pass; bool indices, float bounds, and explicit stride slicing reject. Sealed base-type rejection is also covered by intrinsic and authority cases.

quote: No other instance attribute access is permitted in project code.
notes: Declared record field reads pass; nonrecord attributes and undeclared record fields reject.

quote: Argument unpacking with `*` or `**` is prohibited.
notes: Positional and keyword binding pass; star arguments reject. Double-star coverage is provided by frontend unsupported-syntax fixtures, not claimed exhaustive here.

quote: Dynamic format specifications, locale-sensitive formatting, arbitrary `__format__`, `repr`, and object formatting are prohibited.
notes: Primitive formatting passes; dynamic format spec, locale format, repr conversion, and unconverted bytes reject. Arbitrary object-format dispatch is also excluded by exact inserted-expression types.

quote: List, dictionary, set, and generator comprehensions are prohibited in PurePy 0.1.
notes: Explicit approved loops pass; all four comprehension families reject.

quote: For example, `len(value)` is accepted only when `value` is exactly `str`, `bytes`, or `tuple[T, ...]`.
notes: Tuple/string len calls pass while a record operand rejects; bytes len is also covered by the existing intrinsic fixture.

quote: The verifier MUST version and test the intrinsic table. Adding an intrinsic is a language change.
notes: The table is coupled to verifier version/cache identity. make differential-test now checks the documented operator/intrinsic verdict matrix and inferred exact types against CPython 3.14, including typed empty tuples, domain failures, and permanent regression controls. The finite matrix is not exhaustive, and an independent explicit intrinsic-table version is not yet release-frozen.

quote: Every call target MUST resolve to exactly one callable declaration.
notes: Unique direct declarations resolve; duplicate top-level callables, unknown imported symbols, and computed targets reject.

quote: Every argument MUST match the exact declared parameter type and category.
notes: Explicit optional widening and exact direct capability/reference forwarding pass; bool/int mismatch and nominally different authority fail.

quote: Capability and host-reference values may only appear as direct call arguments.
notes: Original parameters forward directly; aliases, tuples, comparisons, and formatting reject. Section 8.6 lists each category exclusion.

quote: A verifier MUST reject any attempt by a pure function to call an effectful function, even if dead-code analysis would suggest that the call is unreachable.
notes: The checker visits calls even after return. A pure caller cannot manufacture the required capability/reference arguments for the unreachable external call.

quote: The verifier MUST NOT resolve call targets through runtime registries, dependency-injection containers, decorators, route tables, import hooks, module `__getattr__`, or monkey-patched names.
notes: Direct resolution plus rejected computed targets, decorators, and mutation cover representative ambient resolution mechanisms. No dedicated runtime registry/import-hook differential matrix is claimed.
